title: Completeness of the BLR linearity test
statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ be a linear function, meaning $f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then the BLR acceptance probability of $f$ equals $1$; that is,
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y)\bigr] = 1,
\]
where $x$ and $y$ range independently and uniformly over $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$.
hypotheses_covered: k is a positive modulus (NeZero k)
f is linear: f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y) for all x,y
replaced:
If $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is linear, then
$\Pr[{\rm BLR\ accepts}\ f] = 1$.
